name: Kinaxis Maestro
positioning: Public, Canada-based supply chain planning leader known for patented concurrent-planning technology (Maestro, formerly RapidResponse) that lets large enterprises simulate and recalculate their entire supply chain in near real time.
strengths: Patented concurrency engine — near-instant what-if recalculation across the full network
Deep reference base in high-tech, life sciences, aerospace/defense, and industrial manufacturing
Public-company scale, balance sheet, and long enterprise track record
Frequently cited for the fastest scenario analysis at enterprise scale
weaknesses: Long, services-heavy implementations typical of legacy concurrent-planning deployments
Configuration-first UX that often requires dedicated planning-ops staff to maintain
Not built on a CRM platform — commercial/sales-pipeline data has to be integrated in, not native
Premium enterprise pricing that can be hard to justify below large deal sizes
pricingNotes: Enterprise subscription, typically multi-year, sized to network complexity and user count. (Illustrative — confirm against current deal intel.)

name: o9 Digital Brain
positioning: Markets the "Digital Brain" — a graph-based, AI/ML-powered platform spanning demand, supply, and integrated business planning, positioned as a strategic, cross-functional planning layer for large global enterprises.
strengths: Graph-based data model built for large, complex, cross-functional planning scenarios
Strong analyst and enterprise mindshare in strategic IBP / demand-supply integration
Broad SI partner network (EY, Genpact, valantic, and others) for global rollouts
Marquee global brand logos across beauty, CPG, and industrial sectors
weaknesses: Large, platform-scale implementations with long time-to-value
Heavy reliance on SI/consulting partners to configure and roll out
Not natively unified with CRM/commercial systems — requires integration to connect sales data
Premium enterprise pricing aimed at large, multi-year transformation budgets
pricingNotes: Enterprise subscription, typically bundled with SI implementation services. (Illustrative — confirm against current deal intel.)

name: Blue Yonder Luminate Planning
positioning: Panasonic-owned end-to-end supply chain suite spanning demand and supply planning through warehouse and transportation execution — a single-vendor "plan to execute" story.
strengths: Broadest single-vendor footprint from planning through warehouse / transportation execution
Large existing retail, CPG, and manufacturing installed base
Regular new-logo momentum (dozens of new customers reported per quarter)
Panasonic-backed scale and balance sheet
weaknesses: Breadth-over-depth critique — planning is one of many priorities inside a very large suite
Historically complex, services-heavy implementations
Suite-wide upgrades and roadmap can move slower than focused planning-only vendors
Not CRM-native — commercial pipeline/opportunity data isn't a first-class object in the platform
pricingNotes: Enterprise suite licensing, often multi-module bundles. (Illustrative — confirm against current deal intel.)

name: SAP Integrated Business Planning
positioning: SAP's cloud supply chain planning suite, positioned as the "safe default" for the 1,000+ companies already standardized on SAP ERP — covering S&OP, demand, inventory, and response/supply planning natively alongside S/4HANA.
strengths: Native fit for SAP-centric IT landscapes — the path of least resistance for SAP shops
Deep bench of SAP implementation partners and talent
Bundling leverage inside broader SAP enterprise agreements
Continual platform investment (Excel-based planning UX, embedded AI features)
weaknesses: Best-of-breed capability gaps versus concurrent-planning and AI-native specialists
Perceived as slower-moving and harder to configure than newer entrants
Value proposition narrows sharply outside SAP-standardized landscapes
Not built for CRM-linked or commercial-signal-driven planning workflows
pricingNotes: Typically bundled into broader SAP cloud / enterprise agreements. (Illustrative — confirm against current deal intel.)

name: Anaplan Supply Chain Planning
positioning: Flexible, modeling-first "connected planning" platform used broadly across finance, sales, and supply chain — supply chain teams build planning apps on top of Anaplan's general-purpose Hyperblock calculation engine.
strengths: Extremely flexible, build-your-own-model platform — can be shaped to almost any planning process
Strong existing footprint in FP&A that supply chain can piggyback on for a single-platform pitch
Large partner / consulting ecosystem for custom model-building
Long track record of supply chain wins across CPG, retail, and industrial accounts
weaknesses: General-purpose platform, not purpose-built for supply chain — planning logic must be custom-modeled
Model build and maintenance typically requires dedicated Anaplan modeling expertise
Best-of-breed supply-chain-specific features (concurrency, network optimization) are thinner than specialists
Private-equity owned (Thoma Bravo) — roadmap priorities can shift with portfolio strategy
pricingNotes: Per-user / per-workspace enterprise licensing. (Illustrative — confirm against current deal intel.)

name: Logility Digital Supply Chain Platform
positioning: Long-standing supply chain planning specialist, now part of Aptean, pushing "DemandAI+" and agentic AI features, and consistently well-rated in Gartner Voice of the Customer for supply chain planning.
strengths: Strong customer satisfaction — 2025 Gartner Voice of the Customer recognition with high willingness-to-recommend scores
Purpose-built supply-chain-planning heritage (demand, inventory, S&OP) rather than a repurposed general platform
Newer agentic AI push (DemandAI+, Intelligent Order Response) aimed at mid-market and enterprise
Backed by Aptean's broader ERP / vertical-software portfolio and go-to-market
weaknesses: Smaller market profile and brand awareness than Kinaxis / o9 / Blue Yonder in competitive enterprise deals
Aptean acquisition integration is still relatively recent — roadmap and packaging can be in flux
Less concurrency / scenario-simulation depth than Kinaxis at extreme enterprise scale
Not CRM-native — commercial data has to be integrated separately
pricingNotes: Subscription licensing, positioned competitively for mid-market and enterprise. (Illustrative — confirm against current deal intel.)
